newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says Syria should rein in Hizbollah. [CORRECTED 12:28 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says Syria should rein in Hizbollah. [CORRECTED 12:28 GMT]

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday it would be impossible to forge peace with Syria unless Damascus reined in Hizbollah guerrillas fighting Israeli troops in south Lebanon.
Visiting an Israeli army base on the Lebanese border, Netanyahu said it "would not be wise" for any side to set conditions for the resumption of Israeli-Syrian peace talks.

"But it is clear that for negotiations between Israel and Syria to make progress there must be direct and determined Syrian action to reduce terror here," he said, referring to Hizbollah attacks in Israel's occupation zone in Lebanon.
"It is impossible to advance peace between Israel and Syria if an indirect war against Israel is being waged here," Netanyahu said.
Syria is a main powerbroker in Lebanon and Israel has repeatedly demanded it crack down on the Iranian-backed Hizbollah.
Netanyahu flies to Washington on Wednesday to plot future Middle East peace moves with Israel's closest ally.
Officials expect that U.S. President Bill Clinton will commit to seeking a "bridging formula" for restarting peace talks with Syria severed by Israel nearly a year ago.
During his trip to northern Israel, Netanyahu also visited some of the seven Israeli soldiers wounded on Sunday in a Hizbollah attack in south Lebanon.
Nearly 200 soldiers have died fighting guerrillas in Lebanon since Israel set up its occupation zone in mid-1985 (corrects from mid-1995).
Last week, 73 Israeli soldiers were killed in the collision over the Galilee of two military helicopters carrying them to south Lebanon.
